doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

title: Opening and the long partnership with Houston Person
summary: Rowe opens the filming; Jones describes 31 years with Houston Person as a working marriage, with Houston calling the songs.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive on the Hamilton campus. And I’m very pleased to have Etta Jones, vocalist, with me today. I’m looking forward to having you visit.
Welcome. You’re in town for a performance with Houston Person.
And you guys have a long performing relationship, almost thirty years, is that right?

Those are the best kind, but not always, they don’t always happen. We were just talking, when you guys get your repertory together for certain kinds of gigs, do you each bring something to the table? You know, “I’d like to do this tune,” and work it out?

No. At first, when we first started working together I used to like maybe write a list you know. But after a while that just went to nothing and Houston started calling the songs, because I didn’t want to take my break to write lists to sing. And I couldn’t think of anything to sing. It got so — you forget what you actually — what songs you actually do. And he can call them in a minute.
I’m glad you said that. I have that same problem, remembering the songs that you know.
